description: The COMPUTED styles of one element — colour, type, spacing, border, shadow, layout — plus its box in CSS pixels, and the CSS custom properties (design tokens) in scope for it. This is how you check a built page against a design: it answers "this button renders #3B82F6 at 15px with 22px padding" without a screenshot and without measuring anything by eye. Target it by a qa_snapshot ref (preferred) or a CSS selector. Read-only and executes NOTHING: the property list is fixed in the extension, so you name an element, never a program. Pair it with a design source (a Figma file, a token JSON) to report the diff, and with qa_spotlight to show the human which element you mean.

frameId.description: Which frame to ask, from qa_frames. Omit for the page itself. A payment form, an SSO step or an embedded widget usually lives in a frame of its own, and a cross-origin one can only be read from inside it.

ref.description: A ref from qa_snapshot (e.g. "e12") — preferred over selector

tabId.description: Target tab (from qa_tabs); omit for the active tab

tokens.description: Include the CSS custom properties in scope (default true)

name: qa_styles
title: Computed styles and box of an element
